title: Principality of Jersika
capsule: The Principality of Jersika (Gerzika / Zargrad) was a medieval Latgalian principality on the right bank of the Daugava in what is now eastern Latvia, one of the largest indigenous polities in the region before the Northern Crusades. Its ruler Visvaldis practiced Eastern Orthodox Christianity and maintained ties to Polotsk, but in 1209 Bishop Albert of Riga and the Livonian Brothers of the Sword defeated him in battle, forcing him to accept his own kingdom back as a fief while losing Autīne and Cesvaine. After Visvaldis died around 1239 the territory passed entirely to the Livonian Order and the Bishopric of Riga.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's general location is confirmed by chronicle sources and archaeology, but its precise territorial extent relative to neighboring Latgalian polities is only approximately known.
